# Best RV power station and solar combo

The results don't include bundle prices, so I'm pairing stations with panels based on solar input limits. The right choice depends on whether you'll run a roof air conditioner.

## Top picks

**1. Best overall for RVs: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3**
- 4,096Wh (expandable past 12kWh), 4,000W continuous and 8,000W surge. That's enough to start a 13,500 BTU roof AC, which draws about 1,500W running and spikes past 3,000W at startup.
- Charges 0-80% in about 50 minutes from a wall outlet.
- It's heavy (a two-person lift) and the most expensive once you add batteries.
- Details: https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/

**2. Best value with a built-in RV port: BLUETTI AC200L**
- 2,048Wh, 2,400W output, 1,200W max solar input, and a 30A RV outlet. It weighs about 62 lb.
- Details: https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/ and https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/

**3. Biggest capacity for the money: ALLPOWERS R4000**
- 3,456Wh LiFePO4, 3,600W continuous (6,000W peak), an RV outlet, and 2,000W of solar input across three inputs. It has a 5-year warranty and weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb).
- The listed price is $1,499. With code EXTRA12 (12% off orders over $1,200, expires 2026-11-15), the site tested it at $1,319.12. Code ALLPOWERS26 gives 10% off ($1,349.10) through 2026-12-30.
- Reaching the full 2,000W of solar requires panels on all three inputs, since each input tops out at 650W.
- Buy: https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh (affiliate link). Source: https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh

**Lighter use (weekends, fridge, Starlink, no AC): Jackery Explorer 1000 Plus** at 1,264Wh and about 14.5 kg. It pairs with a 200W solar suitcase. Source: https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife

## Solar pairing
- **Check the station's solar input limit first.** A big panel array is wasted if the station caps input below it. For example, the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 caps at 400W, while the Bluetti AC200L accepts 1,200W. Source: https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life
- **Panels:** a 300-400W folding array can refill a mid-size unit in a full day of decent sun (https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/). NomadSignal suggests the Renogy 200W Foldable Solar Suitcase for smaller setups (https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife).
- **Rooftop panels:** for the biggest stations, rooftop or multiple panels are needed to use their high solar ceilings.

## Caveats
- I only have a direct purchase link for the ALLPOWERS. For the others, search the model name on the brand's store or Amazon, and confirm current price and specs there.
- Most of these sources earn affiliate commissions, and the EmergencyEnergy guide is written for Ontario, so check any wiring or code advice against US rules. Don't hardwire a station into your RV without a qualified electrician.

If you tell me your biggest loads (roof AC? fridge? Starlink?) and how many nights off-grid, I can narrow this to one pick.
